story.html: Onosato was already an Ozeki when the tracker switched on, and the rest of the climb took him less than a year. He won championships in back-to-back tournaments in March and May 2025, then a third in September 2025, and that last one carried him to Yokozuna. His shikona means "great village," handed down the line from Takanosato and Kisenosato, the master who trained him. He fights in a midnight blue mawashi. Reaching the top rank this fast is rare, and his record across the crew era is the plain explanation for it.

bio.v: 大の里 (Ō-no-sato) = 大 great + の (of) + 里 village → literally 'great village.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on characters, but this is a LINEAGE name: '-nosato' places him in the line of yokozuna Takanosato (隆の里) and his master Kisenosato (稀勢の里); 大 chosen to accentuate his talent.

story.html: Kirishima has done the hard thing in sumo, which is fall and climb back. A former Ozeki, he opened the crew era down at Maegashira 1 in January 2025 and spent most of a year grinding through the named ranks, Komusubi and Sekiwake, again and again. The reward came in March 2026: a championship from Sekiwake, and with it the return to Ozeki, where he has held since. He carries the name of his stablemaster, the former Yokozuna Kirishima, and it means "mist island," which is also a volcanic range in Kyushu. He wrestled his earlier career as Kiribayama. The mawashi is a deep brownish purple.

bio.v: 霧島 (Kirishima) = 霧 (mist) + 島 (island) → 'Mist Island' (also the Kirishima volcanic range in Kyushu). Confidence: HIGH. Lineage: inherited from his stablemaster, former yokozuna Kirishima.

records.note: For Aonishiki, Makuuchi and Crew match, since he reached makuuchi after our Jan 2025 epoch; the three-way split matters most for veterans who fought before it.

story.html: In March 2025, Aonishiki was a Maegashira 15, the bottom of the top division. Eighteen months later he is an Ozeki. The Ukrainian climbed through Komusubi and Sekiwake and collected three championships on the way up: Kyushu 2025 as a Sekiwake, January 2026 on the run that made him Ozeki, and July 2026, where he added a Technique prize after a slip back down to Sekiwake. That July run was the wild one. He fought the whole basho on a bad left toe, took out both reigning Yokozuna on back-to-back days, clinched his Ozeki return, and then won the cup in a three-way playoff, all on the same foot. His shikona reads as "blue brocade," a tip of the cap to his master Aminishiki of the Ajigawa stable, with the blue nodding to the flag he came up under. The mawashi is British racing green. To the crew, he's just AO.

bio.v: 安青錦 (Aonishiki) = 安 + 青 (blue/youth) + 錦 (brocade) → 'Blue brocade.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: honors his master ex-sekiwake Aminishiki (安美錦, now Ajigawa oyakata) — shares the 安…錦 frame; 青 (ao) marks the young Ukrainian himself. The 青 (ao, blue) also nods to his homeland — the baby-blue-and-yellow of the Ukrainian flag. — Jennie, 2026-07-22

story.html: Atamifuji is young and pointed upward. He bounced around the maegashira ranks through 2025, as low as Maegashira 12 that May, then found another gear: Komusubi in March 2026, Sekiwake by May, and he has held the rank through the summer, picking up a Fighting Spirit prize in July 2026 along the way. The name is a hometown flag. "Atami" is the hot-spring town he comes from, and "Fuji" is the mountain, so the shikona reads as Atami's Fuji. He wears a dark, muted raspberry red. The crew calls him Atomic.

bio.v: 熱海富士 (Atamifuji) = 熱海 (Atami, his hometown — lit. 'hot sea') + 富士 (Mt. Fuji) → "Atami's Fuji." Confidence: HIGH. Context: names his hometown Atami; Fuji connotes strength/majesty.

story.html: Hakunofuji arrived as one of Isegahama's most-hyped prospects and has the name changes to prove it. He came up as Ochiai, then took the shikona Hakuoho, a tribute built to evoke Hakuho and the Taiho line. Under that name he climbed to Maegashira 1 by November 2025. He then became Hakunofuji, and the climb continued: from Maegashira 10 in May 2026 up to Komusubi by September, his first time at a named rank. He wears a medium grey-brown mawashi. Still only in his early twenties, he is one to watch.

bio.v: Formerly Hakuoho 伯桜鵬 (伯 + 桜 cherry-blossom + 鵬 great roc) — a documented tribute name evoking Hakuho and the Taiho/Otake line. Now Hakunofuji; current kanji unverified. Confidence: LOW on the current form (the Hakuoho meaning is solid). Isegahama; flag to verify new kanji.

story.html: Kotoshoho already has the thing most men on this page are still chasing: a championship. He won it from Maegashira 15 at the July 2025 basho, the kind of rank-and-file title that upends a tournament. He climbed to Sekiwake by May 2026 on the strength of it before settling back to Maegashira 1 this September. He is the elder Koto brother, Sadogatake through and through, and came up as Kototebakari. His shikona reads as "koto victory peak." He wears a light blue-grey mawashi.

bio.v: 琴勝峰 (Kotoshoho) = 琴 (koto, the harp) + 勝 (victory) + 峰 (peak) → 'Koto victory peak.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: Sadogatake 琴- prefix; brother of Kotoeiho (both surname Tebakari).

story.html: Takayasu is one of the elder statesmen of the division, a former Ozeki still trading with the best of them at Maegashira 2. His July 2026 basho brought a Fighting Spirit prize, by the crew's count his 14th career special prize, won in a two-minute grind over Asanoyama in the Nagoya heat that, oddly, seemed to ease his chronic bad back. One booth note the crew logged: his mawashi is famously tight, wrapped so hard that opponents cannot get a finger or a nail under it, which is a big part of why nobody can find a grip on him. He fights in a dark blue mawashi. Around the crew he is Hairy, or Papayasu.

bio.v: NOMINATION (from Day 15.5 live broadcast): known for an exceptionally tight mawashi — booth: "you can't even get your fingers or a nail in there," which is why opponents struggle to get any grip on him. Crown a Known-For tag if you agree (closest existing tag = Technician).
高安 (Takayasu) = 高 (high) + 安 (peace/ease) — but this is his real surname, so the 'meaning' is incidental. Confidence: MEDIUM (real-name shikona).

story.html: Gonoyama is a powerhouse who has spent the crew era ranging across the maegashira ranks, from a high of Maegashira 2 down to Maegashira 13 in November 2025 and back up to Maegashira 3 this September. The "go" in his name is inherited from his master, the former Ozeki Goeido, now the Takekuma stablemaster, and the shikona reads as "mountain of strength." He came up as Nishikawa. He fights in a midnight blue mawashi.

bio.v: 豪ノ山 (Gonoyama) = 豪 (go, strong/grand) + ノ + 山 (mountain) → 'Mountain of strength.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: 豪 from his master, ex-ozeki Goeido (豪栄道), now Takekuma oyakata.

story.html: Takanosho is a former Sekiwake holding at Maegashira 4, a solid upper-maegashira presence with the pushing-and-thrusting build to trouble anyone on a given day. His shikona reads as "prosperous victory." He came up under the name Masunosho before settling on this one. He fights in a red mawashi.

bio.v: 隆の勝 (Takanosho) = 隆 (taka, prosper/flourish) + の + 勝 (victory) → 'Prosperous victory.' Confidence: MEDIUM.

story.html: Roga has climbed to a career-high Maegashira 5 this September after a crew era spent working through the middle and lower maegashira, with a dip into juryo in early 2025. The Russian-born wrestler fights out of the Futagoyama stable, and his shikona is one of the better ones on the banzuke: "elegant wolf." He came up as Roga Chikara. He wears a dark blue-purple mawashi.

bio.v: 狼雅 (Roga) = 狼 (rō, wolf) + 雅 (ga, elegant/refined) → 'Elegant wolf.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Russian-born, Futagoyama stable.

story.html: Asanoyama is a former Ozeki on the way back. The tracker catches him in juryo in November 2025, and from there it has been a steady climb: Maegashira 16 in January 2026, then up through the ranks to Maegashira 6 by September. His shikona reads as "morning mountain," the "asa" marking him as a Takasago man, and he fought earlier as Ishibashi. He wears a deep plum purple mawashi. A former top-ranker rebuilding in real time is one of the more compelling arcs on the board.

bio.v: 朝乃山 (Asanoyama) = 朝 (morning) + 乃 (poss.) + 山 (mountain) → 'Morning mountain.' Confidence: HIGH. Lineage: Takasago 朝- prefix.

story.html: Fujiseiun spent much of 2025 in juryo before breaking through. By March 2026 he had a maegashira spot, and he has held in the middle of the division since, ranking Maegashira 7 this September. His shikona pairs the Fujishima "fuji" with "seiun," an idiom for lofty ambition, so it reads as something like "wisteria of high aspirations." He fights in a midnight blue mawashi. The climb out of juryo and the name both point the same direction.

bio.v: 藤青雲 (Fujiseiun) = 藤 (wisteria) + 青雲 (seiun, 'blue clouds' — an idiom for lofty ambition) → 'Wisteria of high aspirations.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: Fujishima 藤- prefix.

story.html: Takerufuji comes with one of the great recent debut stories in the sport: he won a top-division championship in his very first makuuchi tournament, a genuine sensation. He sits at Maegashira 8 this September. An Isegahama man, his shikona reads as "noble Fuji," and he came up as Ishioka. He is from Aomori and fights in a medium lilac purple mawashi.

bio.v: 尊富士 (Takerufuji) = 尊 (takeru, revered/noble/exalted) + 富士 (Mt. Fuji) → 'Noble Fuji.' Confidence: HIGH. Isegahama; famous for a sensational 2024 top-division-debut yusho.

story.html: Ura is the one who never sits still on the banzuke. Across the crew era he has bounced from the upper maegashira down into the low teens and back up, no championship and no special prize to his name, and a crowd that couldn't care less about either. What they come for is the way he wins. Ura built his reputation on acrobatic, unorthodox sumo, the kind of bout that ends with an opponent flipped over a hip or marched backward out of the ring by a plan nobody saw coming. The mawashi is cherry blossom pink, which fits him about right. He is one of the older men in the division and still one of the toughest to prepare for.

bio.v: 宇良 (Ura) = 宇 (u, eaves/the heavens) + 良 (ra, good/fine) — his real surname, so the 'meaning' is incidental. Confidence: MEDIUM (real-name shikona). Context: famed for acrobatic, unorthodox techniques.

story.html: Oho carries one of the heaviest names in sumo. He is the grandson of the legendary Yokozuna Taiho, whose name meant "great roc," and Oho inherits the roc, so his own reads as "king roc." On the dohyo he reached Sekiwake and Komusubi more than once across the crew era before a hard slide to Maegashira 10 this September, a drop the crew noted alongside a possible late-July injury. He came up as Naya. He wears a dark purple mawashi. When he is right, the joi is where he belongs.

bio.v: 王鵬 (Oho) = 王 (king) + 鵬 (hō, the giant mythical roc/Peng) → 'King Roc.' Confidence: HIGH. Lineage: grandson of the legendary yokozuna Taiho (大鵬, 'Great Roc') — inherits the 鵬 character.

story.html: Wakamotoharu is a former Sekiwake holding at Maegashira 11, fighting through a nagging lower-back and glute problem that the crew has been watching, the kind of thing that quietly drains a wrestler's forward drive. He is the eldest of the Onami brothers, the youngest being Wakatakakage two spots below him on this banzuke. The "waka" honors their grandfather, a former Sekiwake, and the brothers are named for the three Mori warlords. He came up as Araonami, then Goshi. He wears a black mawashi.

bio.v: 若元春 (Wakamotoharu) = 若 (waka, young) + 元春 (Motoharu, after the Sengoku warlord Kikkawa Motoharu) → 'Young Motoharu.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: eldest of the Onami brothers; waka- honors their grandfather ex-sekiwake Wakabayama, and the brothers' names invoke the three Mōri brothers. Brother of Wakatakakage.

story.html: Wakatakakage has the most bittersweet line on the banzuke. He won the championship in May 2026 from Komusubi, a career peak, and then it went sideways: a serious hip injury right before the July basho forced him out, and the crew flagged it as potentially career-altering. He returns to this banzuke all the way down at Maegashira 12, the fall a direct result of the time lost. He is the youngest of the Onami brothers, with Wakamotoharu just above him here. His shikona reads as "young Takakage," after a Sengoku warlord. He wears a deep navy blue mawashi. The crew shorthand is WKTKKG.

bio.v: 若隆景 (Wakatakakage) = 若 (waka, young) + 隆景 (Takakage, after the Sengoku warlord Kobayakawa Takakage) → 'Young Takakage.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: youngest of the Onami brothers; waka- from grandfather ex-sekiwake Wakabayama; brothers named for the three Mōri brothers. Brother of Wakamotoharu.

story.html: Asakoryu has spent the crew era in the lower maegashira, with a career-high spike to Maegashira 7 in May 2026 before settling back to Maegashira 13. He is a Takasago man and the brother of Asasuiryu, three spots below him on this banzuke, the two of them sharing the "asa" family prefix. His shikona reads as "morning crimson dragon." He came up as Ishizaki. He wears a red mawashi.

bio.v: 朝紅龍 (Asakoryu) = 朝 (morning) + 紅 (crimson) + 龍 (dragon) → 'Morning crimson dragon.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: Takasago 朝- prefix; brother of Asasuiryu (both surname Ishizaki).

story.html: Tobizaru is a former Komusubi holding at Maegashira 14, and his name tells you how he fights: "flying monkey." The style matches it, agile and evasive, built to make bigger men miss. He is an Oitekaze man, with an older brother, Hidenoumi, also in the sport, and he came up as Iwasaki. He wears a light grey-blue mawashi.

bio.v: 翔猿 (Tobizaru) = 翔 (tobi, soar/fly) + 猿 (saru, monkey) → 'Flying Monkey.' Confidence: HIGH. Context: fits his agile, evasive style; Oitekaze (older brother is Hidenoumi).

story.html: Asasuiryu makes his top-division debut on this banzuke, promoted to Maegashira 15 for September 2026 after a run in juryo. He is the brother of Asakoryu, two spots up the banzuke, and the shared "asa" prefix once caused an earlier scoring session to mistake the two of them for one wrestler before the crew sorted it out. A Takasago man, his shikona reads as "morning jade dragon." He came up as Ishizaki. First tournament at this level, so the story starts here.

bio.v: 朝翠龍 (Asasuiryu) = 朝 (morning) + 翠 (jade-green) + 龍 (dragon) → 'Morning jade dragon.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: Takasago 朝- prefix; brother of Asakoryu (both surname Ishizaki).

story.html: Wakanosho is a maegashira wrestler at Maegashira 16 this September, out of the Minatogawa stable. The crew has an open injury watch on him: he withdrew partway through the July 2026 basho, officially with a knee, though the booth had also flagged a possible concussion from a head-first sequence a day earlier, and the crew has deliberately kept both readings on the record rather than reconcile them. He wears a navy blue mawashi.

bio.v: 若 (waka, young) + -nosho; the remaining kanji are unverified. Confidence: LOW — flag to verify kanji. Minatogawa stable.

story.html: Shonannoumi is a maegashira wrestler ranking Maegashira 17 this September, ranging through the lower and middle maegashira across the crew era. The name flags his home coast: Shonan, the stretch of Kanagawa coastline, plus "sea," so the shikona reads as "the Shonan sea." He is a Takadagawa man.

bio.v: 湘南乃海 (Shonannoumi) = 湘南 (Shonan, the Kanagawa coast) + 乃 + 海 (sea) → 'the Shonan sea.' Confidence: HIGH. Names his home coast; Takadagawa stable.

story.html: Hoshoryu spent all of the crew era at the top. He won the Emperor's Cup at the January 2025 basho as an Ozeki, and by March 2025 he was a Yokozuna, where he has ranked ever since. The record has not been all smooth: he withdrew partway through the July 2026 tournament and has fought through stretches on the sidelines. His shikona means "ascending dragon," and the dragon is not decoration. It ties him to his uncle, the former Yokozuna Asashoryu, whose own name carried the same character. He fights in a dark navy mawashi. When he is healthy and forward, there are few better.

bio.v: 豊昇龍 (Hō-shō-ryū) = 豊 abundant + 昇 rising/ascending + 龍 dragon → 'Ascending dragon.' Confidence: HIGH (characters). Lineage echo: the 龍 dragon ties to his uncle, former yokozuna Asashoryu (朝青龍).

story.html: If you want to know what Ozeki consistency looks like, it is Kotozakura's line on the banzuke: Ozeki, every single tournament, start to finish, no dips and no gaps. The championship has not come yet in the crew era, and that is the one thing left on the list. The name is an inheritance. His grandfather was the 53rd Yokozuna, also Kotozakura, and the "koto" is the signature of the Sadogatake stable that every wrestler there carries. He came up as Kotonowaka before taking the family name. The mawashi is a light turquoise green, and the crew calls him "6 Pack."

bio.v: 琴櫃 (Koto-zakura) = 琴 koto (harp) + 櫃 zakura (cherry blossom) → 'Koto cherry blossom.' Confidence: HIGH. Inherited proper name — 琴 koto is the Sadogatake stable signature (all its wrestlers carry it); passed down from his grandfather, the 53rd yokozuna Kotozakura.

records.note: For Fujinokawa, Makuuchi and Crew match, since he reached makuuchi after our Jan 2025 epoch; the three-way split matters most for veterans who fought before it.

story.html: Fujinokawa is one of the youngest men in the division and he has climbed like it. In September 2025 he was a Maegashira 9. A year later he is a Sekiwake, having run up through the ranks with an Outstanding Performance prize at Maegashira 1 in July 2026 as the marker along the way. His shikona means "wisteria river," a name the Isenoumi stable brought back into use, and he fought earlier as Wakaikari. He wears a medium blue mawashi. The crew calls him Bloody Eye.

bio.v: 藤乃川 (Fujinokawa) = 藤 (wisteria) + 乃 (poss.) + 川 (river) → 'Wisteria river.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: a revived Isenoumi-beya shikona.

story.html: Daieisho is a fixture, one of the division's dependable pusher-thrusters. He held Sekiwake through the first four tournaments of 2025, slid back into the maegashira ranks in the autumn, and has worked his way up to Komusubi by September 2026. His shikona reads as "great soaring glory." He came up under earlier names, Takanishi and then Daishoei, before settling on this one. He fights in a dark raspberry red mawashi. Japanese fans know him as the Battle Pug, and once you have seen the low, square, forward style, the name explains itself.

bio.v: 大栄翔 (Daieisho) = 大 (great) + 栄 (glory/flourish) + 翔 (soar) → 'Great soaring glory.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH.

story.html: Kotoeiho spent the back half of 2025 riding the elevator between juryo and the bottom of makuuchi, and then he broke out. A Fighting Spirit prize at Maegashira 7 in July 2026, and a jump all the way to Maegashira 1 for September, his highest rank yet. He is the younger of the two Koto brothers on this banzuke, and the crew calls him the master of shiko: his high, balanced leg-lift stomp is a genuine crowd-pleaser and draws applause on its own. The "koto" marks him as Sadogatake, like his brother Kotoshoho, and he fought earlier as Kototebakari. The mawashi is a medium slate blue.

bio.v: Showman — signature is a beautiful, balanced high shiko (leg-lift foot stomps) that draws big applause; the crew calls him 'the master of Shiko.' Day 7: a beautifully balanced high leg stomp caught the eye again. (Jennie, 26NgD07)
琴栄峰 (Kotoeiho) = 琴 (koto, the harp) + 栄 (glory) + 峰 (peak) → 'Koto glory peak.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: Sadogatake 琴- prefix; brother of Kotoshoho (both surname Tebakari).

story.html: Yoshinofuji reached Komusubi and sits at Maegashira 2 this September, in the thick of the joi. He came up under the name Kusano, ranking in the maegashira ranks through 2025, before taking a shikona in the Isegahama Fuji lineage. The new name reads as "Yoshino Fuji," pairing Mount Fuji with Yoshino, the region famous across Japan for its cherry blossoms. Still in his mid-twenties, he is early in what could be a long run near the top of the maegashira.

bio.v: 吉野富士 (Yoshinofuji) = 吉野 (Yoshino, a region famed for its cherry blossoms) + 富士 (Mt. Fuji) → 'Yoshino Fuji.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Isegahama-beya (Fuji-family shikona).

story.html: Churanoumi has climbed quietly and steadily. He worked through the lower and middle maegashira ranks across 2025 and pushed into the upper maegashira through 2026, reaching Maegashira 2 twice and holding at Maegashira 3 this September. His name is the best kind of hometown flag. He is Okinawan, and "chura umi" is the beloved Okinawan phrase for the beautiful sea, so the shikona simply means "beautiful sea." He fought earlier as Kizaki. He wears a purple mawashi.

bio.v: 美ら海 (Churanoumi) = 美ら (chura — 'beautiful' in Okinawan) + 海 (sea) → 'Beautiful sea.' Confidence: HIGH. Context: Okinawan-born; 'chura umi' is the famous Okinawan phrase for the beautiful sea.

records.note: For Fujiryoga, Makuuchi and Crew match, since he reached makuuchi after our Jan 2025 epoch; the three-way split matters most for veterans who fought before it.

story.html: Fujiryoga is one of the division's newer faces and he has come up fast. He first appears in the tracker at Maegashira 17 in March 2026 and has already reached Maegashira 4 by September, a steep climb for a short window. He is a Fujishima man, the "fuji" (wisteria) marking the stable, and he came up as Goshima. He is from Aichi and fights in a dark blue mawashi. Early days, but the trajectory is worth watching.

bio.v: 藤 (Fuji, wisteria — Fujishima-beya prefix) + -ryoga. Confidence: LOW — the 藤 (Fujishima signature) is solid; the -ryoga kanji are unverified, so the full meaning is a guess. Flag to verify kanji.

story.html: Oshoma reached Komusubi in July 2025 and has settled into the upper maegashira, ranking Maegashira 5 this September. The Mongolian is a weight-forward, driving wrestler by design. As he told the Sumo Salon panel in Paris, he bulked up roughly 40 kilograms in six months to get there, eating three kilos of rice plus sides before bed so he was "never hungry," and now sits around 160 kilograms, which he calls just right for his style. He noted his stablemaster is also foreign-born, so "he understands where I'm coming from." He fights in a light grey mawashi.

bio.v: Oshoma — the -shō-ma likely 勝馬 (victory + horse) → roughly 'victory horse,' but the first kanji is unverified. Confidence: LOW — flag to verify kanji. Naruto stable, Mongolian.

story.html: Ichiyamamoto has spent the crew era as an upper-maegashira regular, topping out at Maegashira 1 in January 2026 and holding around Maegashira 6 this September. He is also one of the division's better characters. He worked as a civil servant before turning to sumo, and on the Sumo Salon panel he became the running "he's the exception" gag: a bread-for-breakfast holdout who loved the Paris croissants, sleeps soundly before bouts, and keeps his distance against Mongolian opponents, thrusting to stay clear of their throws. His name reads as "Yamamoto the First," his real surname with "one" set in front. He wears a jade green mawashi. The crew calls him Sleepy, and Itchy.

bio.v: 一山本 (Ichiyamamoto) = 一 (one/first) + 山本 (Yamamoto, his real surname) → 'Yamamoto the First.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Context: prepends 一 (one) to his real surname.

story.html: Nishikifuji has bounced between juryo and the maegashira ranks across the crew era and sits at a career-high Maegashira 7 this September. He is an Isegahama man in the Fuji family of shikona, and his name reads as "brocade Fuji." He came up as Ogasawara. He wears a light plum purple mawashi.

bio.v: 錦富士 (Nishikifuji) = 錦 (nishiki, brocade) + 富士 (Mt. Fuji) → 'Brocade Fuji.' Confidence: HIGH. Isegahama-beya (Fuji-family shikona).

story.html: Hiradoumi has been an upper-maegashira fixture for the whole crew era, parked around Maegashira 3 for tournament after tournament before easing back to Maegashira 8 this September. His career high is Komusubi. The name flags his home region: Hirado, a city in Nagasaki, plus "sea," so the shikona reads as "Hirado sea." He came up as Sakaguchi. He fights in a midnight purple mawashi.

bio.v: 平戸海 (Hiradoumi) = 平戸 (Hirado, a city in Nagasaki) + 海 (sea) → 'Hirado sea.' Confidence: HIGH. Context: names his home region, Hirado.

story.html: Shishi has worked his way up to a career-high Maegashira 9 this September after a crew era spent in the lower and middle maegashira. He is the division's other Ukrainian, alongside Aonishiki, and one of its bigger men at 192 centimeters. The booth has taken to comparing him to Baruto, the former Estonian Ozeki, for his balance, his fighting spirit, and how much he has improved. His shikona means "lion." He wears a black mawashi.

bio.v: 獅司 (Shishi) = 獅 (shi, lion) + 司 (shi) → 'Lion.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Context: Ukrainian-born (Ikazuchi stable); the shikona both echoes his real name and means 'lion.'

story.html: Kinbozan has ranged across the maegashira through the crew era, as high as Maegashira 3 in July 2025, ranking Maegashira 10 this September. The Kazakh-born wrestler fights out of the Kise stable, and his shikona is a good one: "golden peak mountain," after Kinpozan, a real sacred peak. He wears a grey mawashi.

bio.v: 金峰山 (Kinbozan) = 金 (gold) + 峰山 (peak-mountain; Kinpōsan is a real sacred peak) → 'Golden Peak Mountain.' Confidence: HIGH. Context: Kazakh-born, Kise stable.

story.html: Shodai is a former Ozeki who has spent the crew era bouncing through the maegashira ranks, holding around the middle of the division and ranking Maegashira 11 this September. He is one of the few who fights under his own family name, so the "meaning" of the shikona is really just his surname. He wears a black mawashi. There is still enough of the former top-ranker in him to make trouble on his day.

bio.v: 正代 (Shodai) = 正 (correct/upright) + 代 (generation) — but this is his real surname, so 'meaning' is incidental. Confidence: MEDIUM (real-name shikona). Context: fights under his own family name.

story.html: Asahakuryu is a newer face who rose out of juryo in late 2025 and has established himself in the maegashira ranks, as high as Maegashira 8 in May 2026 and ranking Maegashira 12 this September. The Mongolian is a Takasago man, the "asa" prefix the same one that ran through Asashoryu, and his shikona reads as "morning white dragon." He wears a dark blue mawashi.

bio.v: 朝白龍 (Asahakuryu) = 朝 (morning) + 白 (white) + 龍 (dragon) → 'Morning white dragon.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: 朝 (asa-) is the Takasago-beya signature prefix (cf. Asashoryu).

story.html: Abi is a big pusher-thruster who opened the crew era at Komusubi and has slid down the maegashira ranks over the following year, ranking Maegashira 13 this September. His career high is Sekiwake. When his thrusting attack is on, it is relentless and he can beat anyone; when it is off, the results wander, which is roughly the shape of his crew-era banzuke. His shikona reads loosely as "blaze." He came up as Horikiri. He wears a midnight blue mawashi.

bio.v: 阿炎 (Abi) = 阿 (mostly phonetic 'a'; also 'nook') + 炎 (flame/blaze) → loosely 'Blaze.' Confidence: MEDIUM — 炎 'flame' is clear, 阿 is largely a sound character.

story.html: Chiyoshoma is a wily veteran, a Kokonoe man ranking Maegashira 14 this September. The color piece writes itself: in July 2026, on Day 9, he won his bout on his own birthday and recorded his 300th career victory the same afternoon. His shikona reads as "Chiyo's soaring horse," the "chiyo" marking the stable. He came up as Shoma. He wears a golden brown mawashi.

bio.v: 千代翔馬 (Chiyoshoma) = 千代 (a thousand generations) + 翔 (soar) + 馬 (horse) → 'Chiyo's soaring horse.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: 千代 (chiyo-) is the Kokonoe-beya signature prefix.

story.html: Tokihayate is a maegashira wrestler ranking Maegashira 15 this September. He is a Tokitsukaze man, the "toki" marking the stable, and his shikona reads roughly as "swift gale." He came up as Tokisakae.

bio.v: 時疾風 (Tokihayate) = 時 (toki, time) + 疾風 (hayate, gale / swift wind) → roughly 'swift gale.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: 時 (toki-) is the Tokitsukaze-beya signature prefix.

story.html: Toshinofuji makes his makuuchi debut on this banzuke, a new top-division entrant at Maegashira 16 for September 2026. He is an Isegahama man in the stable's Fuji lineage, alongside names like Atamifuji, Midorifuji, and Nishikifuji, and his shikona reads as "Fuji of longevity." First basho at this level, so his story begins now.

bio.v: 寿之富士 — “Fuji of Longevity”: 寿 (toshi/kotobuki, long life & auspiciousness) · 之 (no, “of”) · 富士 (Mt. Fuji). The –富士/–fuji suffix marks the Isegahama-beya shikona lineage (Terunofuji, Atamifuji, Midorifuji, Nishikifuji…).
